Method: Derived from the GNU ld map in evidence/output.map.gz, parsed by cres_t4.service.linker_map.parse. Byte figures are the linker's own accounting, not an estimate. No tool's bill of materials was consulted: a corpus whose truth came from a scanner measures agreement with that scanner.
Matching: A candidate component matches a ground-truth entry when its name, lower-cased with punctuation removed, equals the entry's Name or any of its AcceptableNames. Anything else is a false positive and any unmatched entry is a false negative. Both are named individually in the score, never summarised away.

Components.Name: FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP
Components.VersionNote: No commit was recorded for the built tree, so there is nothing to establish a version from. The map carries no version information -- it never does.
Components.LicenceNote: The project's published licensing. NOT checked against a LICENSE file in the built tree, so it does not meet the protocol's 'independently verified' bar.
Components.Uncertainty: THE SEVEN DISCARDED OBJECTS ARE THE POINT OF THIS CASE. They were compiled -- the build produced object files -- and the linker put none of their bytes in the image: IPv6, DHCPv6, two DNS modules, the IPv4 and IPv6 TCP paths, and Tiny TCP. The component itself shipped, so this entry's Scope is 'shipped'; a tool claiming the DHCPv6 or IPv6 code shipped is wrong, and DiscardedNames is what scope accuracy is measured against.

Components.Name: FreeRTOS kernel
Components.LicenceNote: The project's published licensing, not verified against the tree.
Components.Uncertainty: Six objects of a kernel that has far more: a build selects one port (ARM_CM3) and one heap implementation (heap_3), so the absent ones are a configuration choice rather than dead code. Reporting the kernel once is right; reporting 'FreeRTOS heap_3' as a component is a granularity error, not a false positive, and the score says which.

Components.Name: newlib
Components.VersionNote: The archive paths carry the GCC version (12.2.1), not newlib's own. Establishing it needs the toolchain package's manifest, which was not kept.
Components.LicenceNote: newlib is a COLLECTION under several licences -- BSD variants plus historical terms on individual files -- and naming one would be wrong. A real answer requires reading the tree's COPYING.NEWLIB.
Components.Uncertainty: ONE COMPONENT, TWO ARCHIVES, and that is a judgement. librdimon_nano.a is newlib's semihosting stub library and comes from the same upstream project, so a bill of materials naming 'newlib' once is correct. A tool reporting both archives separately is not wrong about the bytes -- it is answering at a different granularity, and AcceptableNames admits either so this does not register as a false positive. It is also the single largest component in the image at 206KB of 297KB, which is worth knowing before anybody reports this firmware as 'mostly FreeRTOS'.

Components.Name: libgcc
Components.VersionNote: Read from the archive's own path (/usr/lib/gcc/arm-none-eabi/12.2.1/...), which is the compiler's version and in practice libgcc's too. Heuristic rather than pinned because the path is a filesystem layout, not a manifest.
Components.LicenceNote: libgcc's published terms. The runtime exception is the part that matters to a device maker and the part most tools drop, reporting bare GPL-3.0 and implying an obligation that does not apply.

Evidence.PulledInNote: Four members, all integer division helpers the Cortex-M3 has no instruction for.

Components.Uncertainty: Compiler runtime rather than a dependency anybody chose, which is exactly why it is missed: nothing in the source tree mentions it and it is in every image.

NotComponents.Name: the demo application
NotComponents.Why: First-party code -- the echo client and its startup. Five objects, 7,225 bytes, under build/ with no upstream. A tool reporting these as third-party components is producing false positives, and the score counts them as such.

Open.Question: Is the LAN9118 Ethernet driver its own component?
Open.Detail: smsc9220_eth_drv.o (1,722 bytes) sits under FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP/source/portable/NetworkInterface/MPS2_AN385/ether_lan9118 -- vendor driver code vendored inside the network stack's portable layer. It is currently counted inside FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP. A device maker auditing for a vulnerability in that driver would want it named. Resolving this needs the upstream provenance, which needs the recorded commit.

Open.Question: Does the total reconcile?
Open.Detail: 67453 + 6822 + 206111 + 9416 = 289802 across the four components, plus 7225 of first-party code = 297027, which is the map's own LinkedBytes. It reconciles exactly, and a case whose bytes do not reconcile is a case whose truth is not established.
